title: Simchat Torah close: the circle
hookLine: the Torah's last letter and first letter spell lev, heart; the scroll rolls straight on

lines: THE LAST WORDS, THEN THE FIRST.
cards: On Simchat Torah, synagogues get loud. The scrolls come out of the ark and people dance with them, around and around the room, seven circuits, sometimes spilling out into the street. Children wave flags.

Someone who hasn't set foot inside all year is handed a scroll to hold. And in the middle of all that, something quiet and precise happens at the reading table. The last words of the Torah are read aloud.
And then, without stopping, the first.

teach.b: Deuteronomy ends with the words in the sight of all Israel; in Hebrew, le'einei kol Yisrael. So the last letter of the whole Torah is the lamed at the end of Yisrael.
Genesis begins with bereshit, in the beginning, and its first letter is bet.
Put the last letter and the first together, lamed and bet, and they spell lev: heart. Some teachers point this out. The Torah, end joined to beginning, makes a heart.

On Simchat Torah, the person honored with reading the end is called the chatan Torah, the bridegroom of the Torah. The one honored with starting again is the chatan Bereshit, the bridegroom of the beginning.
The scroll isn't rolled up and put away for a rest.

teach.h: ROLLED STRAIGHT BACK TO THE START.
teach.b: It's rolled straight back to its start, and the same day the reading begins again: "In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth."

Since day three hundred thirty-two, this path has walked from the plagues in Egypt through the rest of Exodus, through Leviticus and Numbers, and these last weeks through Deuteronomy, Moses' farewell.
The forgotten sheaf and the first fruits. Choose life. Write your own.
The song, the blessing, the grave no one knows, face to face. Tomorrow a new part of the year begins: the siddur, the prayer book, walked page by page. But the Torah doesn't stop.

how: On Simchat Torah, congregations dance with the Torah scrolls in seven circuits (hakafot), read the end of Deuteronomy, and immediately begin Genesis again; the two readers are honored as chatan Torah and chatan Bereshit, and some communities honor women with parallel titles.

o: light: the first thing God makes in Genesis
law: the Torah's very last word, in Hebrew
heart: the Torah's last and first letters

games.q: inside the circle — tap the pairs.

s: after the last verse, the scroll is put away until the next week
it's rolled back and Genesis is read the same day.
the Torah's last and first letters together spell lev, heart
lamed from Yisrael, bet from bereshit.

games.q: on Simchat Torah you've just heard the last verse of Deuteronomy read. what happens next at the reading table?
o: the scroll is closed for a month.
the last verse is read again.
games.why: the chatan Bereshit is called up and 'in the beginning' is read straight away: no gap at all.

practice: Say the end of the Torah, Moses' mighty deeds, done in the sight of all Israel, and then its beginning, in the beginning God created the heaven and the earth, one after the other with no pause in between.
Notice what it's like to finish and start in the same breath, and where something ending in your own life might touch a beginning.

wordCard.voice: Lev. Heart — the word spelled when the Torah's last letter and its first letter are joined, on the day the ending touches the beginning.
